chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Forming his own band and the Barnes Tavern job
summary: After leaving Armstrong in spring 1937 he organized a band; John Hammond visited while Mosley broadcast on WNEW.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Let's get to the time when you leave Louie's band around sometime in the spring of '37.
Spring of '37.
Aside from Lil, now this is the time when you begin your own career as a bandleader, how did this Barnes Tavern thing come about; that seems like a very unlikely place.
I organized the band and I'm trying to remember who it was that booked me in there--
Was it John Hammond?
No. Johnny was one of the first guys to come up and see me, but he didn't have anything to do with the booking.
At the time that Johnny Hammond came up there, I was on that program, the WNEW program Around The Town. I used to broadcast over that program.
I had Taddy Smith--
Taddy was acquired from
Basie's band.
Yeah.
He was a wild man.
Yeah, we almost had a run in.
He was hard to get along with.
He was;we almost had a fight.
He was a good trumpet player though.
Yeah, he was a very good trumpet player.
We had Skeets Tolbert on sax and Freddy Jefferson--
The piano player Freddy Jefferson?
Yeah. I think Freddy was on piano.
Was John Brown playing bass with you?
No, no.
Not that early.
No, he wasn't with me that early.
